anya (ml-eng): quick summary of the SSE vs WS runs across GPUs/regions. tested model-x v1 (2.7B), seq=128, prompt ~60 tokens. endpoints: streaming (SSE) and websocket (WS). regions: us-east1 / eu-west1 / ap-southeast1. GPUs: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L4. batching varied 1..8 concurrency. TL;DR: SSE edges out WS at sustained >500rps on A100/H100 due to streaming amortization; WS slightly lower p50 at low rps but has p99 spikes under large batch sizes.
liam (infra): nice. what payloads / tokenization did you use? any difference for longer contexts?
anya (ml-eng): tokenizer = gpt2-bpe, avg input tokens=60, gen tokens=64. we also tried seq=512 for one sweep (higher mem). long context increases batching variance; SSE still amortizes better because incremental token emission avoids big tail lamdas for KV cache flushing.
maria (bench): pasted raw numbers from the dashboard (numbers are medians across 3 runs):

A100 (us-east1):
- SSE @ 800rps: p50=32ms p95=86ms p99=140ms throughput=760rps
- WS  @ 200rps: p50=28ms p95=120ms p99=260ms throughput=190rps

H100 (eu-west1):
- SSE @ 900rps: p50=29ms p95=82ms p99=130ms throughput=860rps
- WS  @ 220rps: p50=25ms p95=110ms p99=240ms throughput=210rps

L4 (ap-southeast1):
- SSE @ 300rps: p50=48ms p95=180ms p99=420ms throughput=270rps
- WS  @ 80rps:  p50=42ms p95=210ms p99=520ms throughput=70rps

anya (ml-eng): quick interpretation: SSE wins when you can sustain higher concurrent requests because streaming emits tokens as they're produced and reduces effective tail. WS has lower fixed overhead for a single short request, so p50 is slightly better at low load but p99 suffers when batches grow and scheduling contends.
liam (infra): what about kernel selection? we saw different perf between cutlass/tensorir/triton kernels last month.
anya (ml-eng): good call. we ran kernel=auto vs pinned. results: on H100 pinning cutlass for matmul gave ~8% lower p99 for non-streaming endpoint; on A100 autotune picked a mix (cuBLAS+triton) that was best for throughput. for L4 triton kernels + int8 path reduced latency but quality dropped a hair.
liam (infra): can you paste the command snippets used so I can reproduce the WS vs SSE clients?
anya (ml-eng): sure — minimal reproducer:

```
# SSE client (curl)
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d '{"model":"model-x","input":"...","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate

# simple WS (wscat)
wscat -c "wss://api.redwood.internal/v1/ws" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# then send: {"model":"model-x","input":"...","stream":true}
```

dev-bot: uploaded chart: https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/1769702468/stream-ws-sse-plot.png :bar_chart:
sarah (prod-sre): these p99 numbers on eu-west1 H100 look good, what's the recommended capacity planning if a customer expects 1k sustained rps with 99.9% p99 SLA?
anya (ml-eng): rule of thumb from these runs: reserve ~25-30% headroom beyond observed throughput. for H100 in eu-west1 A100-equivalent cluster, 1k sustained rps -> provision for 1.3k target capacity. use larger pools with continuous batching enabled and keep streaming enabled for that route. set fallback policy to lower-cost non-streaming variant if queue latency grows.
maria (bench): also note quantization effects: int8 paths increased throughput by ~30% on L4 but raised word-level quality regressions ~0.7 BLEU-ish (small). int4 gave 60% throughput uplift but quality regressions visible for code/completion workloads — flag for evals.
liam (infra): action items: (1) replicate H100 pinned-cutlass run in eu-west1 with seq=512, (2) add kernel selection flag to the per-route config in staging, (3) surface a streaming vs non-streaming toggle in the console with perf hints. i'll file infra tickets.
anya (ml-eng): sounds good. i'll add a short writeup with a concise recommendation table and attach latency-by-rps curves. thanks team. :white_check_mark:
